title: Haloumi Nuggets and Wedges
subtitle: with Peas and Sweet Chilli Sauce
description: We love haloumi pan-fried, we love it in burgers and salads, but have you tried it baked? Seriously, these salty nuggets of cheese coated in crunchy breadcrumbs are to die for! Round off the meal with sweet potato wedges and peas.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C. Line 2 oven trays with baking paper. Cut the unpeeled sweet potato into 1cm-thick wedges. Drain the haloumi and dry on paper towel. Halve the haloumi horizontally, then cut each piece into quarters. Cut half the lemon into wedges.

Bake sweet potato: Put the sweet potato on a lined tray, drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to combine. Bake on the upper oven shelf, turning halfway, for 25 mins or until golden and tender.

Crumb haloumi: Meanwhile, put 2 tsp plain flour in a shallow bowl. Whisk 1 egg in a shallow bowl. Combine the breadcrumbs and Italian seasoning in a separate bowl. Dust the haloumi with the flour, shake off the excess, then dip in the egg and coat in the breadcrumb mixture.

Bake haloumi: Put the haloumi on the remaining lined tray. Bake on the lower shelf for 10 mins or until golden. Meanwhile, bring a small saucepan of water to the boil for the peas. Add the peas to the pan, return to the boil and cook for 1 min or until tender. Drain.
Serve up: Divide the crumbed haloumi, sweet potato wedges and peas among plates. Serve with the sweet chilli sauce and lemon wedges. Enjoy!
Did you know?: Panko are the Japanese version of breadcrumbs (panko means 'small pieces of bread'). They're lighter and larger than regular breadcrumbs, producing a much better crunch.
